items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The main two that I – that were very important in my life – was Milt Hinton and Truck Parham.

ctx.x: Who were some of the early influences? Because you’re really catching up to speed on the bass and . . .

Yeah. I had great help as far as my development on the instrument from very, very, very competent musicians, bass players. The main two that I – that were very important in my life – was Milt Hinton and Truck Parham. They were both excellent bass players, and they [were] patient and good teachers. They realized that I had a lot of natural ability, so it made it easier for
the training I got from them. They helped me in every way. They’re working. Something came up. If they thought I could handle it, they’d call me.

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: His wife Gladys, his first wife Gladys and I graduated from high school together, you know and we were all friends.

ctx.x: Well I’ve been in Carnegie Hall many a time and I’ve played there and felt very lucky to meet many great people, you know, Streisand and all them. But I’ve never felt like I felt that night cause we’d come, we’d come all the way, I’d seen it all the way. With John Levy you know. His wife Gladys, his first wife Gladys and I graduated from high school together, you know and we were all friends.
Well just tell me something. Did you get a chance to get any, just a taste of Louis Armstrong playing with Lil Armstrong and the boys that came, the fellas that came from New Orleans?

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Milt Hinton had sort of, we were in school together and Milt had sort of helped me develop that instrument.

ctx.x: Tell us how you moved from — you’re a musician yourself.

Yeah. Well my story is all accidental I call it. I guess I was the type of person who was always interested in the business end of music, right from the very beginning. And I got into it sort of like, as I say accidental, because I had studied violin and then I sort of picked up bass, and Milt Hinton had sort of, we were in school together and Milt had sort of helped me develop that instrument. And I was actually working in the post office and just gigging on the side, because I got married very young so I had a…
Don’t quit your day gig, right?
